methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Amca, founded by Jai Malik and Eli Giovanetti, is a robotics and manufacturing company preparing for IPO. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of 9 robotics and manufacturing peers—1 public (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. Amca has raised $76.5M to date.

The peer-median method is not applicable here. Despite identifying 10 same-sector peers in robotics and manufacturing, none satisfy narrow filtering criteria: zero companies match both stage and valuation tier, zero match adjacent-stage classifications, and zero fall within comparable valuation bands. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial selection bias and mask material differences in business model, maturity, and addressable market across the peer set. This methodological gap reflects the heterogeneity of the robotics sector and the paucity of IPO-stage comparables with sufficient overlap to Amca's profile.

Without sufficient narrow-peer triangulation, this valuation framework cannot support a single point estimate or tight range. Key uncertainties driving valuation include (1) the relevance of the single public comparable to Amca's operations and growth profile, (2) late-stage private fundraising multiples among the eight private peers and their applicability, and (3) revenue trajectory and unit economics for an IPO-stage robotics firm. A complete valuation would require either expanding the comp set via adjacent sectors or employing DCF and precedent transaction methods to ground the range.
